text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 1: No planned contrast found lagged power changing day-ahead error significantly'
text.tspan: Figure 1: No planned contrast found lagged power changing day-ahead

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Lagged power means a lag: the power at the same clock hour on an earlier whole day. Day-ahead means lead-day 1, the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. An arm is one forecast configuration. Each planned contrast, P1 to P5, is a treatment arm minus a reference arm. P1: L1 minus B0. P2: AN minus L1, on the last 8 months only. P3: S2 minus L2. P4: L1 minus B0 scored on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), approximated from nine quantiles (0.1 to 0.9). P5: L1 minus B0 in one XGBoost model shared by all plants. The other rows are scored on mean absolute error. Dot: estimate. Line: 99% interval from resampling whole months. Zero: no change. Each row names its reference arm's own error. The words at the right of a row give the verdict from both settings. Dots and lines are drawn at both settings. The primary hyperparameter setting is the default XGBoost setting. The sensitivity setting uses shallower trees and stronger regularisation. Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. AN: the analogue ensemble, the power on the 5 recent days whose forecast clear-sky index (the forecast's irradiance relative to clear sky) was closest to the target day's. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
text.tspan: Lagged power means a lag: the power at the same clock hour on an earlier whole day. Day-ahead means lead-day 1, the
forecast for the day after the day it is issued. An arm is one forecast configuration. Each planned contrast, P1 to
P5, is a treatment arm minus a reference arm.
P1: L1 minus B0. P2: AN minus L1, on the last 8 months only. P3: S2 minus L2. P4: L1 minus B0 scored on the
continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), approximated from nine quantiles (0.1 to 0.9). P5: L1 minus B0 in one
XGBoost model shared by all plants. The other rows are scored on mean absolute error.
Dot: estimate. Line: 99% interval from resampling whole months. Zero: no change. Each row names its reference arm's
own error. The words at the right of a row give the verdict from both settings.
Dots and lines are drawn at both settings. The primary hyperparameter setting is the default XGBoost setting. The
sensitivity setting uses shallower trees and stronger regularisation.
Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the
forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). L2: L1 plus that hour's weather
forecast. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. AN: the
analogue ensemble, the power on the 5 recent days whose forecast clear-sky index (the forecast's irradiance
relative to clear sky) was closest to the target day's.
All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.
